subject: Clarifying Redwood's model-improvement opt-out, EU residency, and subprocessor attestations
messages:
From: Samuel Park <sam.park@acadiahealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Acadia Health Legal <legal@acadiahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Clarification on model improvement opt-out + EU transfer requirements

Camila,

Thanks for the demo last week — Acadia is excited by the latency/cost profile, but Legal has flagged a few items we need clarified before we proceed to procurement. High level: we need a contractual commitment that customer content will not be used to improve models (training or fine-tuning) and clarity around prompt/response ownership and cross-border transfers. Specific asks:

- Can Redwood commit to a no-model-improvement (no-train) clause for Acadia data in the hosted product?
- If not, what are the technical safeguards (prefix-only caching, scrub/PII tokenization, retention windows)?
- Where are tokens/data at rest for EU customers — can you guarantee eu-residency for logs and backups?
- Provide a current subprocessor list and attestation that subprocessors won't use Acadia content to train models.
- Evidence: we need an ops runbook / audit artifacts (logs, deletion records) to verify no-training commitments.

We attached our initial DPA redlines for your review (Acadia-DPA-redlines-20270121.pdf). Could you respond with what you can commit and what requires an alternative deployment (Dedicated/Private)?

Samuel Park
Senior Counsel, Acadia Health
sam.park@acadiahealth.com

--- Attachment: Acadia-DPA-redlines-20270121.pdf (pdf)
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Park <sam.park@acadiahealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jan 2027 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarification on model improvement opt-out + EU transfer requirements

Samuel — thanks for the clear list. I'll address each point and outline operational next steps below. TL;DR: we can provide contract-level no-model-improvement commitments and operational evidence, but the strongest guarantees come with Dedicated or Private deployments. For Hosted, we offer an opt-out workflow and technical controls that meet common enterprise needs.

1) No-model-improvement commitment
- Contract: Redwood will add a clause that customer input and generated outputs will not be used to train or improve models without explicit customer consent ("no-derivative-learning"). This is available to customers on both Hosted (with opt-out turned on at account level) and Dedicated/Private (default no-learning).
- Implementation: for Hosted opt-outs we tag customer requests at ingress and exclude them from any model-improvement pipelines.

2) Technical safeguards (Hosted)
- Prefix-only KV caching: only model state necessary for low-latency inference (KV cache) is temporarily stored and is not retained for training.
- Token scrubbing: PII-sensitive tokens can be redacted client-side or we can apply token-level redaction at the edge prior to entering persistent logs.
- Retention windows: by default customer request metadata and logs for accounts with opt-out are retained for 30 days; deletion is automated and recorded in the audit trail.

3) EU residency
- Data-at-rest and backups: For EU accounts we route request logs and artifacts to our EU region (eu-west-1) by default. Persistent backups and audit logs for eu-designated accounts remain in-region unless explicit migration is requested.
- Note: some ephemeral telemetry for service health may be aggregated in the control plane; we can scope that to non-content telemetry for eu opt-outs.

4) Subprocessors and attestations
- Attached: redwood-subprocessors-202701.pdf — current list withDeclared subprocessor commitments and SOC2/ISO links where available.
- Attestation: we can provide a signed subprocessor attestation for Acadia (Ops will generate a dated PDF) showing subprocessors will not use Acadia content for model training.

5) Evidence / ops runbook
- Attached: no-train-ops-playbook.pdf describes the steps for request tagging, exclusion from training pipelines, deletion records, and the audit artifacts we provide (deletion hashes, KMS key rotation logs, request-id retention logs).
- We can provide periodic (quarterly) evidence bundles for enterprise customers or ad-hoc evidence for audits.

Deployment options and trade-offs
- Hosted + opt-out: fastest to stand up; covers contractual no-train and ops evidence, but requires account-level opt-out and our runbook-based attestation.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity; no-learning can be default and we can grant more direct access to logs and per-request artifacts.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): strongest guarantee — customer controls the compute and data plane; Redwood's control plane can be limited to metadata.

Next steps
- I'll schedule a 30-min sprint call with our security/compliance lead to run through evidence expectations.
- We'll prepare the subprocessor attestation and a proposed DPA clause for your legal team to review.

If you'd like, we can have an internal redline of your attached DPA and send a tracked change version by EOD Monday.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com

Thanks Camila — that addresses many points. A few follow-ups before we lock in:

- Contract language: we need explicit "no-derivative-learning" and a clause stating Acadia retains ownership of prompts and model outputs (we're not assigning IP to Redwood). Please include both in the DPA amendment.
- Evidence cadence: quarterly evidence bundles are fine, but we would like an SLA for delivery (e.g., 10 business days after request).
- Subprocessors: we need the attestation and any planned subprocessor changes to be notified 30 days in advance.

Can we do a 30-min call Monday 10:00-10:30 ET to go over DPA redlines and the attestation format? If not, propose alternate times and we'll confirm.

Samuel
